development_trial_findings._note: Findings from the D31/T0068 DEVELOPMENT trial on 172.21.60.23. Recorded because each one contradicts something that was previously assumed or asserted, and an assumption that survived because nobody measured it is the failure mode this project keeps hitting.
development_trial_findings.nrestarts_is_not_boot_evidence: systemd's NRestarts counter RESETS on a manual `systemctl restart`, so a service that crash-looped 596 times during a boot can report NRestarts=0 minutes later. Per-boot restart counts must be derived from the journal (`journalctl -b N -u UNIT | grep -c 'Scheduled restart job'`), not from NRestarts. On the 2026-08-16 22:01 boot: scd 596, edged 16, acctd 8, hotel-admin 7, netd 2, portald 0, caddy 0 -- while five of those units showed NRestarts=0.
development_trial_findings.phantom_postgresql_service_ordering: stayconnect-{netd,scd,pmsd}.service all declared After=postgresql.service. No such unit exists on this appliance (Postgres is the stayconnect-pg container) and systemd silently ignores After= on a missing unit, so the ordering was a no-op in every one of them. FIXED: removed, and netd -- the only one that connects to the DB during startup -- got a bounded readiness gate that always exits 0.
development_trial_findings.svc_edged_had_no_iam_v2_commerce_grants: The Phase-2 commercial-packages admin surface returned HTTP 500 because svc_edged had never been granted anything on the iam_v2 commerce tables. FIXED with table-and-verb-specific grants (deploy/gatep/svc-edged-phase2-commerce-grants.sql); revisions get INSERT and deliberately no UPDATE, so revision immutability is enforced by the database.
development_trial_findings.numeric_grant_overrides_were_unpublishab: decodeJSON lacked UseNumber, so numbers inside free-form map[string]any bodies decoded to float64 while the commerce validators accept only json.Number/int/int64. EVERY numeric grant override sent over HTTP was rejected as invalid_grant_tier: no package with a bandwidth or quota override could be published through the API at all. Invisible because the commerce tests build json.Number in Go and never cross the HTTP decoder. FIXED and regression-tested at the decoder.
development_trial_findings.dsn_gated_tests_were_not_merely_skipped_: Five commerce tests are gated on PHASE2_TEST_DSN, so `go test ./...` reported ok while they skipped. Run against a real scratch database they did not merely skip -- the fixture had drifted four NOT NULL columns behind public.guest_networks and could not insert a row. Three now pass; two still fail and are NOT claimed as passing.
development_trial_findings.voucher_auth_is_served_by_LEGACY_not_iam: MEASURED, not inferred. With STAYCONNECT_IAMV2_MASTER=true and STAYCONNECT_IAMV2_VOUCHER=true, redeeming a voucher through the real scd pipeline (/v1/sessions/authorize) incremented public.sessions 24->25 and left iam_v2.sessions, iam_v2.auth_contexts, iam_v2.devices and iam_v2.entitlements ALL unchanged. iam_v2.auth_contexts is 0, so no IAM-v2 auth context has ever been created on this appliance. The flags being true is NOT evidence that IAM-v2 is the authority for guest authentication here; it is not. What IS proven to run on IAM-v2 is the Phase-2 commerce ADMIN surface (plan and package publication, verified against iam_v2 tables under least-privilege grants). The IAM-v2 guest chain (auth_context -> commerce packages -> quote -> confirm -> entitlement -> session) remains UNEXERCISED.

The flags claimed IAM-v2 owned guest authentication; the code did not -- scd read the flags, constructed an Authenticator, and both real entry points went on calling the legacy pipelines. Before: a voucher redemption moved public.sessions 24->25 with every iam_v2 table untouched. After: an ACCOUNT login through /v1/sessions/authorize-credentials returns authority=iam_v2 with an auth_context_id and device_id, public.sessions stays at 26, and iam_v2.auth_contexts 0->1, devices 2->3, device_network_appearances 0->1. The chain then continues on IAM-v2: offer_quotes 1->2, purchases 8->9, entitlements 8->9, still with public.sessions unchanged at 26. A wrong password returns AUTH_DENIED/invalid_credentials from iam_v2.
development_trial_findings.iam_v2_had_no_credential_issuance_at_all: The runtime had an IAM-v2 authentication domain and NO IAM-v2 issuance path anywhere: every admin route wrote legacy credentials, and the only INSERTs into iam_v2.guest_access_accounts in the whole repository were test fixtures. So ACCOUNT was enabled and authenticating against a table nothing could populate. Issuance now follows the same authority switch (iam_v2 or legacy, never both). VOUCHER issuance is NOT implemented: iam_v2.vouchers requires an envelope-encrypted code (code_ciphertext, code_nonce, code_key_generation_id) and voucher_code_key_generations is empty, so VOUCHER currently fails closed.
development_trial_findings.five_more_privilege_gaps_same_class: Each found only by exercising a path nobody had exercised: svc_scd had no privileges on the iam_v2 auth tables; the auth_contexts trigger calls p3_controlled_operation_open, a DIFFERENT function from the opener, so granting the opener alone still failed; the device_network_appearances upsert needed UPDATE, which PostgreSQL reports as a bare 'permission denied for table'; svc_scd had nothing on the guest commerce read tables; and the confirm step calls the p4 entitlement kernel functions, which needed EXECUTE. Two further PRE-EXISTING faults surfaced in the PostgreSQL log, both silent behind healthy-looking services: svc_acctd could not read public.guest_networks (once a second, degrading accounting attribution), and three of four services could not write public.appliance_service_health at all -- the table an operator would consult to decide whether the appliance is healthy was being written by nobody.
development_trial_findings.production_transition_strategy_remains_O: A source comment in data-plane/cmd/scd/authsec.go asserted that the Product Owner had decided on a CLEAN IAM-v2 REPLACEMENT, that IAM-v2 is the only IAM authority and that the legacy IAM is disposable. Those are D30's clauses, which D31 explicitly withdrew as never approved. The comment has been corrected. The PRODUCTION IAM transition strategy is OPEN: no replacement, migration, dual-run or legacy-retirement approach is authorized, and wiring a repository for a DEVELOPMENT trial is not a transition decision.
development_trial_findings.legacy_plan_dependency_removed_from_iam_: IAM-v2 account creation required a legacy ticket_templates row ('guest access plan'), validated and then discarded. IAM-v2 does not model access that way: what a subject may acquire is decided by PACKAGE ELIGIBILITY RULES evaluated at listing time, and iam_v2.guest_access_accounts has no template column at all (only an optional assigned_package_id). The requirement changed no IAM-v2 behaviour and existed only so the legacy UI form still submitted -- hidden split authority. Removed under IAM-v2 authority rather than replaced with an invented rule of the same shape; legacy issuance keeps it unchanged.
development_trial_findings.account_admin_lifecycle_is_split_authori: MEASURED, not inferred, and it is a defect introduced by switching CREATE to IAM-v2 without the rest of the lifecycle. GET /edge/v1/guest-accounts returns the LEGACY accounts (ahmed, devguest1) and does NOT return the IAM-v2 accounts (devguest2, devguest3) created moments earlier through that same API. So an operator creates an account under IAM-v2 authority and it immediately disappears from the admin UI, while the accounts they can see are ones IAM-v2 will refuse to authenticate. Create writes iam_v2; list, get, update, enable/disable, password reset, delete and disconnect all still read and write public.guest_accounts. This must be closed before the IAM-v2 account surface can be called usable, and it is the reason the capability ladder places the account admin lifecycle under NOT_EXERCISED rather than VERIFIED.
development_trial_findings.voucher_key_model_corrected_from_checkpo: The previous resume checkpoint proposed reusing /etc/stayconnect/secrets/voucher_hmac.key directly as the blind-index HMAC key. Re-reading the FINAL contract key hierarchy showed that is wrong twice: it skips the generation record the schema requires (so nothing rotates and no voucher can name the key that indexed it) and it collapses the encryption and indexing roles onto one physical secret. The file was retired, not reused. Recorded because a plausible checkpoint assumption nearly became the implementation.
development_trial_findings.voucher_issuance_placement_follows_the_k: Issuance was first written in edged because that is where the admin route terminates, and it failed at runtime with the DEK unreadable: edged runs as the unprivileged stayconnect user, the DEK is root-only. The fix was NOT to loosen the key's permissions but to move issuance to scd, which is root and unix-socket only, with edged proxying. The route terminating somewhere is not a reason to put the root of voucher confidentiality there. Grants were corrected to follow the code and svc_edged's overreach revoked.
development_trial_findings.further_preexisting_privilege_gaps_seen_: Observed while diagnosing something else, NOT yet fixed: 'permission denied for schema public' on CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS edge_installed_updates and edge_executed_commands. Some service attempts to self-create those tables at runtime and cannot. Recorded rather than silently ignored; root cause not yet established.
development_trial_findings.voucher_rotation_and_cache_defects_FIXED: Three defects, all in code I had shipped with comments asserting the opposite. (1) The blind index was computed under the ACTIVE generation only, so after a rotation every unredeemed voucher became permanently unfindable; the comment claiming older generations stayed usable 'through their own stored indexes' was a non-sequitur, since a stored index only matches if you compute with the same key. Lookup now supplies one candidate index per generation, newest first, including superseded ones. (2) The opened keys lived in a package-level cache with no tenant/site key, so on a multi-site appliance one site's key would be served to all -- fail-closed but a total voucher outage for every site but one, and invisible on a single-site appliance. Now keyed by (tenant, site). (3) Rotating for real then exposed that ensureVoucherKeyGeneration hardcoded generation 1 for the no-active-generation branch, so the first supersession broke issuance forever while issued vouchers kept working; it now uses max+1.
development_trial_findings.runtime_ddl_removed_rather_than_granted: FIXED. scd ran CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for edge_installed_updates and edge_executed_commands on every start and failed every time with 'permission denied for schema public', discarding the error. The tables already existed, so nothing broke and nothing surfaced it either. The fix was to stop asking, not to give a data-plane service DDL rights on public: both call sites now check to_regclass and disable their channel if the table is genuinely missing, since a silently absent command ledger would break exactly-once execution. Verified: zero schema-permission errors after restart, both channels subscribed.
development_trial_findings.enforcement_plane_was_inert: netd had neither the Phase-3 flags nor NETD_PHASE3_PRODUCER_UID while acctd was already submitting shaping plans, so netd logged unauthorized_producer on every plan; then its writer boundary refused to run because svc_netd had no USAGE on iam_v2 at all. No session could ever be promoted from PENDING_ENFORCEMENT. Both fixed; enforcement now promotes sessions to active and withdraws leases on disconnect.
development_trial_findings.accounting_was_silently_not_writing: With a live, shaped session, acctd logged 'absolute counter observation refused ... permission denied for function ingest_absolute_counters' once per second while accounting_records stayed at 0. svc_acctd lacked the grant; it had been given to svc_netd, which references the function but is not the caller. acctd does not crash on the refusal, so only watching the log under live traffic surfaced it.
development_trial_findings.voucher_single_use_was_never_enforced: Vouchers that had been fully redeemed into live entitlements were all still UNUSED: nothing performed the UNUSED->REDEEMED transition, so one code could be redeemed repeatedly. Found by a post-reboot negative test. Fixed in the same transaction as the entitlement grant.
development_trial_findings.portal_told_guests_they_were_online_when: The voucher and account portal handlers parsed the legacy session_id/duration_seconds reply and redirected to /success. Under IAM-v2 that reply carries auth_context/device/guest_network and NO session, so both fields unmarshalled empty and the guest was sent to '/success?s=&t=0' -- told they were connected at the moment they had only authenticated. The trust boundary (opaque HttpOnly cookie, server-held pins) already existed in commerce.go and was never issued because IAM-v2 auth was dark. Fixed by adding the issuer plus package selection and acquisition; /success is now reached only after a session exists.
development_trial_findings.activation_trusted_the_device_from_the_r: Found by adversarial probe: an arbitrary device_id with a real entitlement id activated a session and consumed a device slot on someone else's grant. The accepted Phase-3 grant path derives device identity from the connection and says explicitly it is 'never from the body'; the new activation endpoint trusted the body. The socket is root-only so a browser could not reach it, which is an argument for the caller being careful, not for the boundary being absent. Activation now requires the device to match the entitlement -> purchase -> auth_context acquisition chain.
development_trial_findings.dsn_commerce_suite_status: 5 of 6 TestCommerceAdmin tests now pass against a real database (was 3 when the fixture was first made to run at all). The remaining failure is the checkout-grace defect above and is genuine, not a fixture gap.
development_trial_findings.grace_typed_keys_are_stated_by_the_schem: The reconciliation was mechanical once the contract was read as authoritative, but the first attempt still guessed: it mapped grace_minutes onto the typed duration because that is the friendlier spelling. grace_config_no_dup_policy_keys enumerates exactly which keys are typed columns, and grace_minutes is not among them -- it is free-form. Treating it as typed made {\"grace_minutes\": 30} look like a partial typed override and get refused by the all-or-none rule, a rule working correctly on an input that should never have reached it. The schema stated the answer.
development_trial_findings.activation_identity_completed: Binding the device to the acquisition chain was necessary but not sufficient: a caller could still present that device with another MAC or on a network it had never appeared on. Device identity in this domain IS (tenant, site, appliance, MAC), and the session is enforced on the bridge derived from the source IP, so both are now checked. The IP itself is deliberately not pinned because DHCP reassigns it legitimately within a network and the source IP is already server-derived rather than taken from the body.
development_trial_findings.appliance_schema_diverges_from_canonical: RESOLVED -- provenance established, and it is NOT drift. data-plane/migrations/0001_edge_init.up.sql (the EDGE migration set the appliance applies, 0001 through 0047 per schema_migrations) creates public.tenants with slug and name NOT NULL, and sites with code and name. CI's Phase-3 disposable PG16 does not apply 0001_edge_init at all; it builds only the narrower iam_v2 subset those suites need, which is why tenants.slug does not exist there. Two different, both-canonical scopes. The checkout integration fixture is written against the CI subset, so its bare INSERT INTO public.tenants(id) is correct there and cannot work against a full edge schema. My earlier error was treating a scratch database cloned from the APPLIANCE as the reference for what canonical looks like; that fixture change was fully reverted.

iam_v2_capability_ladder._note: Precision on purpose. 'The flag is enabled' says nothing about whether a surface works -- that conflation is what let guest authentication run entirely on legacy while three IAM-v2 flags were true. Every capability below is placed on one rung and no capability may be described in prose at a higher rung than it sits here. IMPLEMENTED = code exists. ENABLED = configured on the DEVELOPMENT appliance. EXERCISED = actually run against the live appliance. VERIFIED = run AND confirmed by database/runtime row evidence, not HTTP status. ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED = cannot be proven here without fabricating state.
VERIFIED: ACCOUNT authentication is IAM-v2-authoritative at /v1/sessions/authorize-credentials: auth_contexts, devices and device_network_appearances all increment and public.sessions does not move
IAM-v2 guest commerce chain to ENTITLEMENT: eligible packages, quote, confirm, purchase, entitlement, with the pinned package-revision grants (2048/1024 kbps, 2 devices, 3600s) carried into the quote
IAM-v2 guest-account ISSUANCE through the supported admin API, writing iam_v2 only and never legacy
Legacy fallback is impossible while a method is enabled: a valid LEGACY voucher is denied by iam_v2, is NOT consumed, and creates no public.sessions or public.guests row
Auth-context creation is counted as scd_iamv2_auth_contexts_created_total and NOT as sessions_started
Boot convergence: all seven services at 0 restart jobs and 0 failures, journal-derived

IAM-v2 ACCOUNT admin lifecycle on one authority: list/get/patch/set-password/disconnect/delete all read and write iam_v2 only. Behavioural loop proven -- an admin PATCH enabled=false makes scd deny that account with both the correct and a freshly reset password, and re-enabling makes the new password authenticate.

IAM-v2 VOUCHER issuance and redemption on the accepted key-generation model: per-generation HMAC key sealed as hmac_key_ciphertext under a DEK named by encryption_key_id, AEAD code ciphertext/nonce pinned to code_key_generation_id, AAD bound to owner tuples, only last4 in the clear. A code issued through the real admin API authenticates at /v1/sessions/authorize (auth_contexts 4->5, public.sessions unchanged at 26); a valid LEGACY voucher is denied invalid_code, stays unused and creates no legacy session.

IAM-v2 voucher key ROTATION: generation 1 superseded and generation 2 minted; a voucher issued under generation 1 (S45FV9JV) and one issued under generation 2 (4ZWFS66A) BOTH authenticate, with public.sessions unchanged at 26. Superseded generations remain usable for already-issued vouchers.

IAM-v2 SESSION-AFTER-GRANT end to end: entitlement -> device admission -> iam_v2.sessions -> netd promotion to active. iam_v2.sessions moved 8->13 across the session while public.sessions stayed at 26 throughout.

RUNTIME ENFORCEMENT MATCHES THE PINNED REVISION: nft authorizes the guest IP on br-g90 and the tc class runs at 2048Kbit, exactly the pinned service_plan_revision down_kbps; a third device is refused MAX_DEVICES_REACHED limit=2 against the pinned max_concurrent_devices.
RECONNECT is idempotent: the same device re-activating returns its existing session (reused=true) rather than consuming a second device slot.
ADMIN DISCONNECT against REAL sessions: admin view reported active_devices=2 from live IAM-v2 session state, disconnect ended both with end_reason=admin_disconnect, and netd withdrew the nft lease.
AGGREGATE_ONLINE_TIME accrues: consumed_online_seconds advanced against the pinned 3600s quota with time_accounting_mode=AGGREGATE_ONLINE_TIME.
SINGLE-USE VOUCHER REDEMPTION: first redemption flips the voucher to REDEEMED; a replay is refused not_redeemable with exactly one entitlement on that voucher.

REBOOT (boot b716e9b7): all seven services 0 restart jobs and 0 failures, enforcement plane up with zero producer/boundary refusals, BUILD_ID and flags intact, and BOTH the voucher and account journeys re-proven to an active enforced session afterwards.

PORTAL TRUST BOUNDARY: authentication no longer redirects to /success. An IAM-v2 reply issues the server-side commerce session behind an opaque HttpOnly cookie and sends the guest to package selection; /packages and /packages/acquire refuse with no cookie and ignore forged pins in the query string; the pins never appear in the token or redirect; a legacy reply is untouched; an expired cookie stops working.
VOUCHER KEY ROTATION IS IMMEDIATE: with generations 1 and 2 superseded, a generation-3 voucher issued and redeemed with no wait (previously the cache made new-generation vouchers fail for up to 60s).

SESSION ADMISSION IS BOUND TO THE ACQUIRING DEVICE: a foreign device_id on a real entitlement is refused DEVICE_NOT_ON_ENTITLEMENT and gains no session; forged and non-ACTIVE entitlement ids are refused ENTITLEMENT_UNUSABLE.

ACTIVATION VALIDATES THE WHOLE TRUSTED IDENTITY: wrong MAC on the right device is refused DEVICE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH; an IP resolving to no guest network is refused NO_GUEST_NETWORK; a device belonging to another tenant/site is refused; a coherent identity activates.

PORTAL SUCCESS MEANS ENFORCED: activation waits for netd's promotion, bounded by the caller's deadline, and reports the state observed (enforced=true state=active, matching the database). The portal shows /success only on an enforced session, and SessionsStarted increments only for a session that reached active.

HOSTILE REVIEW: 0 iam_v2 sessions without an entitlement; every active session (7, across 7 distinct devices, both VOUCHER and ACCOUNT) has exactly one nft authorization -- none claims active unenforced; public.sessions=26 and no legacy session created in over 3 hours (newest 06:18, before the authority switch); no IAM-v2 code path writes public.sessions and no branch falls back to legacy.

CHECKOUT-GRACE save -> read -> save is idempotent: the typed grace columns are projected back on read, so an ordinary admin edit cannot publish NULLs over the grace policy. Proven by a round-trip test that writes typed fields plus a free-form key, reads them back, writes the read value, and asserts the typed policy survived.
GRACE PACKAGE PROVENANCE is enforced: the contract's is_system = true requirement is now validated, and a non-system package carrying the CHECKOUT_GRACE type is refused grace_package_not_system.
DSN-gated commerce suite 8/8 against a real database.
Governance mutation-suite BASELINE passes at exact head (structural=PASS keyword=PASS) with sandbox fidelity verified over 1364 files.

DELIVERY PROTOCOL corrected: generate-change-manifest --staged reads the INDEX, so packs must be staged BEFORE generation and validation must run AFTER the delivery commit -- validating earlier agrees with a HEAD the manifest was not written for, which is how a locally-green manifest failed GitHub Governance.

NORMAL CHECKOUT GRACE is system-provisioned per Site and hidden (D32/T0069): the package converges at startup with is_system=true, active, CHECKOUT_GRACE, price 0; it is absent from the operator catalogue; an operator publish carrying package_type is rejected and creates no non-system CHECKOUT_GRACE package; deactivating the system package is refused while an ordinary package stays operator-controlled; and an operator sets POLICY successfully with the typed field landing in its column and the free-form key in the jsonb. post_closure_corrections.title: portald dropped the guest's verification value before forwarding it to scd
post_closure_corrections.classification: POST-CLOSURE CORRECTIVE DEFECT FIX. It corrects the guest-portal forwarding hop. It does NOT reopen, extend or re-evaluate Phase 3 or any closed phase; Phase 3 remains ACCEPTED AND CLOSED at verified DARK maturity (D16/T0024) and MERGED (D17/T0025).
post_closure_corrections.discovered: 2026-08-24, by a Product-Owner test from a real guest device on the PRE-LIVE guest network.
post_closure_corrections.symptom: Room sign-in returned the uniform guest failure. scd logged reason `incomplete_evidence` three times; no auth_resolution row was created, because the resolver was never reached with usable evidence.
post_closure_corrections.root_cause: cmd/portald/pms_phase3_handlers.go phase3In named only room, last_name, reservation_number and request_id. The portal script sends `verification` for room_any and `first_name` for room_firstname. Both were decoded into nothing and forwarded as nothing — silently, with no error at any layer — so scd received a room with no evidence beside it. room_any and room_firstname were therefore incapable of ever succeeding on the real guest path; only room_lastname and room_reservation worked.
post_closure_corrections.why_tests_missed_it: Every existing test called scd's handler directly. None crossed the portald hop, so the hop was the one part of the path nothing asserted. The new coverage exercises the hop itself.
post_closure_corrections.introduced_by: The room_any work (PR #32) added the field to the portal script and to scd and did not update phase3In. room_firstname had the same gap from the start.
post_closure_corrections.merged: PR #43 merged to master as 1482890aa1519651ff37e59352fe59eba88f4053 on 2026-08-25, with all four required checks SUCCESS on head 006a7434d02938e6543d81b9ccd25de2b7996e9c (governance, phase3-full-software-gate, phase4-financial-core-gate, phase5-post-stay-transfer-gate).

deployed.component: portald ONLY. No other runtime component was built, deployed or restarted.

post_closure_corrections.deployment_verification: Three checks, none of which required PMS traffic or a guest authentication. (1) The installed artifact's sha256 equals the locally built one byte for byte. (2) The deployed binary contains all four verification keys - verification, first_name, last_name, reservation_number - and the binary it replaced contained neither `verification` nor `first_name`, which is the defect itself, visible in the shipped artifact. (3) A loopback POST carrying a `verification` field decoded cleanly and stopped at `device_not_on_guest_network`, the device check that sits AFTER decoding and BEFORE the scd hop: proof the new field shape is accepted, and proof the probe never reached scd or the PMS. Counters after the deploy: auth_resolutions unchanged at 8 (latest still 2026-08-23), purchases 0, entitlements 0, sessions 0.
post_closure_corrections.still_unproven: The guest-visible portal path remains unproven end to end. The fix is verified by regression coverage across the portald->scd hop and by the deployed artifact's behaviour, NOT by a real sign-in: the PMS link is intentionally disconnected, so no authentication is possible and none was attempted.
